title: Defending Our Lands and Environment: Protecting the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Worldwide
content:
Statement on International Day of the World's Indigenous Peoples

Each year on 9 August, the international community marks the International Day of the World's Indigenous Peoples, honouring the first session of the UN Working Group on Indigenous Populations in 1982. This year, the CIVICUS global alliance of civil society organisations and activists dedicated to strengthening citizen action around the world reaffirms our solidarity with the more than 476 million Indigenous peoples across 90 countries. They continue to defend lands, cultures, and ways of life in the face of escalating threats.

Indigenous peoples are among the most effective guardians of the world's remaining biodiversity, safeguarding an estimated 80% of it on lands they steward, despite formally holding rights to only a fraction of the territory traditionally occupied. Yet Indigenous human rights defenders and environmental activists who defend these lands remain among the most targeted civil society actors on the planet.

title: Morocco: Provide safety and justice for Sahrawi activist Naama Asfari
content:
CIVICUS calls on Moroccan authorities and the international community to provide safety and justice for Sahrawi human rights defender (HRD) Naama Asfari. While welcoming reports that he ended a 47-day hunger strike on 24 July 2026, we remain deeply concerned about his health and well-being. He has been unjustly detained in Kenitra Central Prison in Morocco. Asfari’s case continues to demand close international attention. 

Naama Asfari has spent more than 15 years in detention following his arrest in connection with the 2010 Gdeim Izik events. His case has been the subject of extensive scrutiny by international human rights mechanisms. The United Nations (UN) Committee against Torture found that he had been subjected to torture and ill-treatment and called for effective remedies. The UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention determined that his detention is arbitrary and called for action consistent with international law.

title: Bangladesh: Two years after the mass protests, civic space is under attack
content:
CIVICUS global civil society alliance warns of faltering civic space under the new Bangladeshi government. Evidence suggests that the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) is further restricting civic freedoms. It has also failed to enact reforms proposed by the interim government which replaced former PM Sheikh Hasina’s regime following mass protests two years ago.  

Human rights defenders are extremely concerned about the decreasing space to speak up or undertake activism since the February 2026 elections, which brought the BNP government to power.  Many have been silenced due to fear of reprisals by both state and non-state actors.  

The BNP government has failed to meaningfully reform the police and notorious Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) which was weaponised under the previous regime to silence all forms of dissent. Further, there has been no reforms to the NGO Affairs Bureau which was used to target critical civil society groups.

title: Joint Letter: Urgent Call to End Escalating Repression in Uganda
content:
Together with partners, we have written to the international community urging immediate action to condemn and respond to the escalating repression of civil society, human rights defenders, journalists and political opposition in Uganda.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

To:  

The United Nations Human Rights Council, Geneva 
The African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights, Banjul 
The African Union Peace and Security Council, Addis Ababa 
The East African Community, Arusha 
The UN Special Rapporteur on Human Rights Defenders 
All UN Member States 

Urgent Call to Action — Condemn and End Escalating Repression of Civil Society, Human Rights Defenders, Journalists, and Political Opposition in Uganda 

THE CONTEXT 

CIVICUS, the global civil society alliance, together with the 246 organisations who signed this letter (with 80 of them who chose to be anonymous), draw urgent attention to the rapid deterioration of civic space and human rights in Uganda. The CIVICUS Monitor currently rates Uganda's civic space as Repressed. This ranking reflects the systematic denial of the freedoms of expression, association, and peaceful assembly.
